title: Rise of universities in Europe
summary: The University of Bologna says its Studium, established around 1088 by tradition, is what turned a village into a medieval metropolis. Teachers such as Irnerius, often mistakenly remembered as the founder, took students into their homes. This outline covers Bologna, often described as the first university in the Western world, as the start of the European university.

uncertainty.note: 1088 is the conventional foundation date established during the 1888 octocentenary; early legal teaching clustered around Irnerius c. 1088 before Frederick I granted the Constitutio Habita in 1155–1158.

where.historical_name: Commune of Bologna, Holy Roman Empire

importance.justification: The emergence of the university as an autonomous corporation of scholars created Europe's enduring institutional framework for higher education, professional law, and academic freedom.

reviewer_note: The 1088 date has been traditionally celebrated for about 150 years. Older centres of learning elsewhere, such as Al-Qarawiyyin and Nalanda, have their own records. The second source is a popular history site.
